content: 1. Rifabutin's effect may be altered due to its interaction with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Nafcillin reduces the efficacy of rifampin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Nafcillin may exhibit antagonistic effects against Staphylococcus aureus. Consider alternative treatments if necessary. 4. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of rimegepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of riociguat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ripretinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors reduces systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially lowering the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 8. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of roflumilast by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Strong CYP450 enzyme inducers reduce systemic exposure to roflumilast, potentially diminishing its therapeutic effectiveness. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Long-term co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inducers with rolapitant may significantly reduce its efficacy. 14. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of romidepsin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided if possible. 16. Nafcillin and rose hips may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Nafcillin and non-ASA salicylates may increase each other's levels due to plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Nafcillin and salsalate may increase each other's levels due to plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Sarecycline reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 23. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 24. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of selumetinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of sildenafil by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Potent CYP3A4 inducers are expected to cause substantial decreases in sildenafil plasma levels. 28. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of silodosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of simvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Nafcillin reduces the effects of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 32. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of siponimod by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Co-administration of siponimod with moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 34. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of sirolimus by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Nafcillin and sodium phenylacetate may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Nafcillin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to activate sodium picosulfate. 38. Nafcillin increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Drugs that induce these enzymes may significantly reduce velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially reducing therapeutic effects. 40. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of solifenacin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of sonidegib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Avoid co-administration of sonidegib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 43. Nafcillin decreases the levels of sorafenib by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of stiripentol by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, increase the stiripentol dose. Monitor closely. 47. Nafcillin reduces the effects of sufentanil SL by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. 49. Discontinuation of concomitant CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentration. 50. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 52. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of sunitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of suvorexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce suvorexant efficacy; if an increased dose is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 55. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tadalafil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of teniposide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of terbinafine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Tetracycline reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 67. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tiagabine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Nafcillin reduces the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 73. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tivozanib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 74. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Loss of or decreased response to tofacitinib may occur when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 76. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tolterodine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tolvatptan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 78. Nafcillin decreases the levels of toremifene by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. CYP3A4 inducers increase the rate of toremifene metabolism, lowering its steady-state serum concentration. 80. Nafcillin reduces the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 82. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of trabectedin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 83. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tramadol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 84. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducers decreases the AUC of tramadol and its active metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol). 85. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of trazodone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 86. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tucatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 87. Nafcillin reduces the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 88. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 89. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 90. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ulipristal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 91. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 92. Avoid co-administration of upadacitinib with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 93. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of valbenazine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 94. Nafcillin decreases the levels of vandetanib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 95. Avoid co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inducers, as these drugs reduce exposure to vandetanib by up to 40%. 96. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 97. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 98. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of venetoclax by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 99. Avoid co-administration of venetoclax with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. Consider alternative treatments with agents that have less CYP3A induction. 100. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of verapamil by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 101. Nafcillin decreases the levels of vilazodone by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
